perspectives.name: discovery-weak-signals

factors.name: governancePower
factors.basis: Nebius's August 2026 AGM disclosed a dual-class voting structure: 238,402,543 Class A shares carried one vote each while 33,455,053 Class B shares carried ten votes each. The same AGM re-appointed Arkady Volozh as executive director and approved five-year board authority to issue additional Class A shares up to 20% of issued share capital and to exclude existing-holder pre-emption rights for those issuances.

risks: The ten-vote Class B structure concentrates voting power relative to economic ownership and can reduce ordinary Class A holders' influence over governance outcomes.

Five-year authority to issue up to an additional 20% of issued share capital, together with authority to exclude pre-emption rights, creates a material dilution/governance option even though it does not establish that shares will be issued.
unknowns: The AGM result does not identify beneficial ownership of the Class B shares or quantify post-AGM voting control by individual holders.
The authorization does not establish timing, price, use of proceeds, or probability of any future Class A issuance.

perspectives.name: expectations-execution

factors.name: capitalExecution
factors.basis: Shareholders approved a five-year board mandate to issue Class A shares up to 20% of issued share capital and exclude pre-emption rights, increasing financing flexibility for the capital-intensive buildout while preserving a measurable dilution risk that Alpha should distinguish from already-executed financing.

risks: Financing flexibility is not realized operating execution; future equity issuance could dilute Class A holders and should not be counted as deployed capital or completed capacity.
unknowns: No issuance under this authorization is evidenced by the AGM result itself.

sources.origin: U.S. SEC EDGAR / Nebius Group N.V. Form 6-K Exhibit 99.1
facts: The AGM had 238,402,543 eligible Class A shares with one vote each and 33,455,053 eligible Class B shares with ten votes each; the classes voted together on all matters.
Arkady Volozh was re-appointed as an executive director with 377,275,928 votes for, 21,732,302 against and 4,071,963 abstained.
Shareholders approved designating the board for five years to issue Class A shares up to an additional 20% of issued share capital (excluding Class C shares).
Shareholders approved designating the board for five years to exclude existing-shareholder pre-emption rights for Class A share issuance.

result: Materially different primary governance evidence packaged for Alpha. It source-addresses governance-power and capital-flexibility/dilution considerations without creating numeric underwriting or treating authorization as executed financing.
